notes: The exchange is stateless: each request is dispatched independently in handle_request (kvstore/src/api.rs:15-33) and no session state is carried between requests, so there are no states to model.

The `put` verb carries a `ttl_secs` field, but it is only parsed and formatted into the stored value (kvstore/src/api.rs:27-28) — no expiry timer exists in the cache (kvstore/src/cache.rs:23-38), so it drives no transition and is not modelled as a timeout.

kvstore/src/storage.rs (FileStore) writes and reads files under a root directory and returns api::Response values (kvstore/src/storage.rs:34-39), but no participant in this revision invokes it — neither main.rs nor api.rs references FileStore — so it is not modelled as a participant.

Transport is in-process rather than networked: the client and store are linked into one binary and communicate by calling handle_request directly (kvstore-cli/src/main.rs:3, 9). The colon-separated request format is nonetheless a wire format this project defines, documented as such at kvstore/src/api.rs:12-14.

protocol.framing: one request per argument string, colon-separated fields (`verb:arg[:arg]`)

messages.name: Response::Ok | Response::Stored | Response::Error
messages.schema: Ok(String) | Stored | Error(String); rendered to stdout with the Debug formatter

participants.description: The kvstore-cli binary. Collects one request string per command-line argument, submits each to the store in order, and prints the returned Response to stdout.
participants.name: client

participants.description: The kvstore api layer. Splits the request on ':', dispatches on the verb, and answers from the bounded in-memory cache.
participants.name: store

protocol.transport: in-process call from the CLI binary; requests arrive as process arguments and responses are written to stdout
